# Flexible Master’s Option

The “Flexible Master’s Option” is a new alternative to our traditional “On-campus Master Option” to conduct Master studies at AIT. It is applicable to selected programs at all of our schools. Students will receive the same degree and the same academic requirements apply as the program offered in our regular “On-campus Option”. Students can do almost all coursework online via AIT’s Hybrid Mode of Instruction (certain programs may require a lab and research work on campus).

## How it Works

Typically, the 1st year is online via AIT’s Hybrid Instruction. Students may spread coursework over more than one year. Students take the same course offered to on-campus students via Hybrid Mode. All classes are recorded for later viewing.

After completion of the coursework, students can do their research or thesis in the AIT Campus at a flexible time.

The application is currently open.

## Payment

First, you need to decide for how many courses you want to enrollee, the minimum enrollment is 6 credits which is equivalent to 2 courses. The Program Secretary can advise you on details. You need to pay the full fee for your courses before the start of the semester.All details to make payments are at this website,Click here.

For the Flexible Master’s Option, apply online at [Application Form](https://ait.ac.th/study/flexible-masters-option/), selecting “Flexible Master Degree” in the program dropdown. You must register for a minimum of 2 courses (6 credits) per semester and a maximum of 15 credits. The fastest completion time is 2 academic years, with a maximum study period of 4 academic years. Payment can be made via money transfer, details available at [Payment Advice](https://ait.ac.th/study/flexible-masters-option/).

For the Open Master of Engineering and Science in Interdisciplinary Studies (OMIS) program, you must submit a Research Plan that includes a title, research field, hypothesis, methodology, facilities needed, impact statement (including potential translation and support for AIT’s goals), and references. The research plan can be in a separate file and uploaded to the application portal.

For the Public Policy Program, the application deadline is 10 May 2026. For further inquiries, contact the Admissions and Scholarships Unit at admissions@ait.ac.th or fpsd_admission@ait.ac.th.

Master’s Program

A master’s program requires 48 credits with two options:

* Option 2: A minimum of 36 credits of coursework and 12 credits of research study

To apply for a master’s degree program at the Asian Institute of Technology (AIT), you must meet the following eligibility requirements:

1. **Academic Background**: Hold a Bachelor’s degree (normally from a four-year program) or its equivalent in an appropriate field of study from an institution of good standing.
2. **Minimum GPA**: Have an undergraduate grade point average (cGPA) of 2.75 or equivalent.
3. **English Proficiency**: Meet one of the following:
   - AIT-EET: 6
   - IELTS Academic: overall 6 (writing 6)
   - TOEFL iBT: overall 80 (writing 21-23)
   - PTE Academic: overall 52 (writing 62-73)
4. **Health and Conduct**: Be in satisfactory physical and mental health and have a record of good conduct.

For the **Flexible Master’s Option**, you can apply online via the [Application Form](https://ait.ac.th/study/flexible-masters-option/) by selecting “Flexible Master Degree” in the program dropdown. You must register for a minimum of 2 courses (6 credits) per semester and a maximum of 15 credits. The fastest completion time is 2 academic years, with a maximum study period of 4 academic years. Payment can be made via money transfer, with details provided on the [Payment Advice](https://ait.ac.th/study/flexible-masters-option/) page.

For the **Open Master of Engineering and Science in Interdisciplinary Studies (OMIS)**, you must submit a **Research Plan** that includes a title, research field, hypothesis, methodology, facilities needed, impact statement (including potential translation and alignment with AIT’s goals), and references. The research plan should be submitted as a separate file.

For the **Public Policy Program (PPP)**, the application deadline is **10 May 2026**. Further inquiries can be directed to the **Admissions and Scholarships Unit** at AIT.

For specific programs like the **Construction Engineering and Infrastructure Management (CEIM)**, applicants should review the course structure and preferred backgrounds for the master’s program.
